article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Honey Banana × Canal Street Runtz
Breeder: Purple City Genetics
THC Content: 29%
CBD Content: Typically very low or trace
Terpene Profile: Limonene , beta-caryophyllene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Honey, banana cream, sugary candy
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Mid to late October
Indoor Yield: High
Outdoor Yield: High under
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Honey Runtz approaches the candy-strain formula from an unusual direction. Instead of relying entirely on berry syrup, citrus candy, or the creamy gas associated with many modern Runtz hybrids, this cultivar introduces an unmistakably nectar-like sweetness that can resemble wildflower honey poured over ripe banana. Purple City Genetics developed the strain by crossing Honey Banana with Canal Street Runtz as part of its El Krem breeding project, a collection built specifically around cannabis capable of combining contemporary flavor with serious hash-making potential.

The result is a resin-heavy, sativa-leaning hybrid with unusually large biomass, approximately 5% reported extraction returns, and a terpene profile the breeder describes in terms of honey, Runtz candy, and banana cream. More recent breeder material places selected Honey Runtz flower above 29% THC, giving this sweet-smelling weed considerably more power than its dessert-like aroma initially suggests.
Genetics and Lineage

Purple City Genetics confirms the lineage as Honey Banana × Canal Street Runtz. Honey Banana supplies the creamy tropical foundation, bringing ripe banana, fruit, sugar, and honey-like qualities into the cross. That parent traces to Strawberry Banana × Honey Boo Boo and has long been valued for both flavor and resin production. Canal Street Runtz contributes a more contemporary candy-and-gas influence along with additional trichome development. The combination was deliberately selected for Purple City Genetics’ El Krem project, which focuses on plants capable of performing as premium dried flower as well as fresh-frozen material for solventless extraction .

Canal Street Runtz itself comes from Pre-64 Runtz crossed with THC Bomb, so Honey Runtz carries several different flavor families beneath its straightforward name. Banana and tropical fruit are inherited from one side, while Runtz candy, cream, berry, and gas arrive through the other. This layered ancestry prevents the finished flower from tasting like a simple banana strain. Instead, the best examples move between nectar sweetness, ripe fruit, creamy candy, berry, citrus, and subtle fuel. Purple City Genetics considered the pairing successful enough to highlight it as one of the central cultivars in its hash-oriented El Krem collection.
Effects and Experience

Despite the richness of its aroma, Honey Runtz generally begins on a brighter note than many dessert-oriented marijuana strains . The first phase can produce an energetic cerebral lift accompanied by improved mood, increased interest in conversation, and a pleasantly creative shift in attention. Music, art, social settings, games, or other low-pressure activities may become more engaging without the immediate heaviness that accompanies strongly sedating weed. Purple City Genetics classifies the plant as a sativa hybrid, and commercial examples of the breeder’s genetics are commonly described as combining euphoria and mental energy with a more relaxed finish.

The body effect becomes more apparent after the initial mental lift settles. Muscles may feel looser, physical tension softens, and the energetic portion of the experience can transition into an easy calm without necessarily producing immediate couch-lock. Dose changes that balance considerably. Flower from the current breeder-selected Honey Runtz El Krem cut has been listed at more than 29% THC, while other commercial flower has tested around 26%. At that level, a few extra inhalations can transform a functional high into a much heavier experience. Experienced consumers may appreciate its combination of stimulation and relaxation, but people with low THC tolerance should approach potent batches conservatively.
Medical Benefits

The progression from cerebral uplift into physical ease may appeal to medical marijuana consumers looking for a cultivar that does not begin with strong sedation. During the earlier portion of the experience, the combination of mood elevation and mental engagement may be useful for people attempting to temporarily manage everyday stress, emotional fatigue, or the difficulty concentrating that can accompany a poor mood. Later relaxation can be more relevant when muscular tension, general discomfort, or an inability to settle down becomes the primary concern.

Honey Runtz should not be regarded as a proven treatment for anxiety, depression, chronic pain, or any other medical disorder simply because consumers associate those symptoms with its effects. Cannabis cultivars are chemically variable, and products carrying the same strain name may contain different cannabinoid and terpene concentrations. High-THC marijuana can also cause anxiety, rapid heart rate, dizziness, dry mouth, red eyes, or temporary impairment in susceptible consumers. Medical use is therefore better guided by the actual laboratory analysis and dose of a particular product than by reputation alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Honey is the signature note, but the aroma has far more depth than the name implies. Fresh flower can release a thick sweetness reminiscent of floral honey or sugar syrup, followed quickly by ripe banana and creamy tropical fruit. Runtz-derived candy appears behind that initial wave, adding berry sweetness and a slightly tart fruit quality. Breaking the buds apart can uncover earth, citrus peel, and restrained gas, preventing the bouquet from becoming cloying. Purple City Genetics summarizes the original El Krem selection with “Honey Runtz” and “banana cream” terps, while its newer clone catalog emphasizes honey, sugar, and Runtz candy.

Individual terpene percentages depend on phenotype and cultivation, but commercial material associated with the Purple City Genetics cultivar has identified limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and myrcene among its prominent terpenes. Limonene can reinforce brighter citrus and candy impressions, beta-caryophyllene contributes peppery warmth and spice, and myrcene adds ripe fruit and earthy depth. When smoked or vaporized, the flavor commonly begins with honeyed banana and sugary tropical fruit before shifting toward berry candy, cream, mild spice, and a faintly gassy finish.
Growing Information

Honey Runtz was bred with production in mind. Purple City Genetics specifically notes large biomass as one of the cultivar’s advantages, an important characteristic for growers producing either flower or fresh-frozen cannabis. The current Honey Runtz El Krem selection finishes in approximately nine weeks indoors, while the breeder lists outdoor maturity from mid to late October. Earlier breeder information similarly places the cultivar within roughly a nine-to-ten-week finishing window.

Vigorous growth means canopy management can improve efficiency indoors. Topping and low-stress training during vegetative growth help spread branches across the available light, while selective pruning can keep crowded interior growth from restricting airflow. A trellis becomes useful once flower weight begins accumulating, particularly when plants are allowed enough vegetative time to develop the large biomass for which the cultivar was selected. Resin production becomes obvious as flowering progresses, making gentle handling increasingly important near harvest.

Hash makers have an additional reason to watch this plant closely. Purple City Genetics reports approximately 5% extraction yield from Honey Runtz, a notable figure that helped earn it a place in the El Krem program. Extraction performance still varies according to phenotype, harvest timing, resin maturity, freezing technique, and processing method, so 5% should be viewed as breeder-reported potential rather than a guaranteed return. Flower growers benefit from many of the same traits: abundant trichomes, strong aroma, sizable plants, and commercially attractive buds.
FAQ
What strain is Honey Runtz?

Honey Runtz is a sativa-leaning hybrid bred by Purple City Genetics from Honey Banana and Canal Street Runtz. It was developed as part of the breeder’s El Krem collection of modern cannabis genetics selected for strong terpene expression and hash production.
Is Honey Runtz indica or sativa?

Purple City Genetics officially classifies Honey Runtz as a sativa hybrid. The experience generally reflects that designation through an uplifting and mentally engaging beginning, although noticeable body relaxation usually develops later.
How strong is Honey Runtz?

Honey Runtz can be very potent. Purple City Genetics lists its newer El Krem clone at more than 29% THC, while commercial flower from the genetics has appeared around the mid-to-upper 20% range. Exact potency varies by harvest, so batch-specific laboratory results should always take priority over a general strain estimate.
What does Honey Runtz taste like?

The central flavors are honey, banana cream, sugary Runtz candy, tropical fruit, and berry. Citrus, earthy spice, and light gas can become more noticeable on the exhale, giving the flavor more complexity than a straightforward sweet strain.
How long does Honey Runtz take to flower?

Indoor plants generally finish in about nine weeks, with some seed-grown expressions potentially extending toward ten weeks. Outdoors, Purple City Genetics lists maturity from mid to late October in suitable Northern Hemisphere growing conditions.
Final Thoughts on Honey Runtz

Honey Runtz is a good example of where modern cannabis breeding is moving beyond THC percentage alone. Purple City Genetics built the cultivar around flavor, resin production, biomass, and versatility, combining the tropical creaminess of Honey Banana with the sweeter candy-and-gas influence of Canal Street Runtz. The finished flower can smell remarkably close to its name, with nectar-like sweetness and banana cream forming the foundation before berry candy, citrus, earth, and gas emerge underneath.

Its horticultural qualities make the strain equally interesting. Large biomass, a roughly nine-week flowering cycle, breeder-reported 5% extraction potential, and THC levels exceeding 29% in selected material create a plant with legitimate appeal to flower growers and solventless hash producers alike. For consumers, the combination of an upbeat cerebral beginning, gradually relaxing body effect, and distinctive honey-banana flavor separates this weed from the seemingly endless collection of conventional Runtz crosses. Honey Runtz retains the candy character expected from the family, but its creamy tropical sweetness and serious resin production give it an identity of its own.
